title: The AI Ledger
introduction: Reviewed through November 23 at 20:00 UTC. GPT-6.2 reaches Chat as a separate rollout, OpenCode adds unattended jobs, and Anthropic and GitHub change enterprise operating details. The November 16–22 edition is archived unchanged. OpenCode already met the previous operational-controls forecast, and verified access still gates direct Mythos 5.2. No fresh timing rumor met the evidence threshold.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Sol variant starts rolling out in ChatGPT Chat
items.summary: OpenAI began a global rollout of a conversation-tuned GPT-6.2 Sol variant in the Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. Enterprise access depends on admin settings.
items.whyItMatters: OpenAI reports improvements on images and complex instructions in its Chat-tab evaluations. Those are publisher results, not independent coding benchmarks.
items.historicalContext: This is distinct from the November 17 GPT-6.2 launch. The November 23 Chat-tab release does not change Work or Codex models, or announce API pricing or subscription-limit changes.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: OpenCode 2.4.0 adds scheduled and event-triggered automations
items.summary: The stable release supports one-off and recurring automations, cron schedules, and events from connected MCP servers. The automation manager exposes the resulting jobs, and the configuration can disable the feature.
items.whyItMatters: Audit what is allowed to run unattended. The release notes say a fixed shell action asks for approval at creation and logs the exit code and output for each run; do not assume it asks for fresh approval at every run.
items.historicalContext: This is a harness release, not a model launch. Its explicit background-task controls meet last edition’s November 23–29 forecast on November 23.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: Anthropic starts Enterprise Frontier Safeguards beta
items.summary: The beta is available for eligible organizations on Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, and Claude Models on Google Cloud when Anthropic-managed. Anthropic says it does not retain prompts or responses under EFS; encrypted safety copies go to a bucket in the customer’s cloud account.
items.whyItMatters: Zero data retention by Anthropic does not mean no copies exist. Workspaces using Anthropic-managed storage do not qualify as EFS. Verify eligibility and storage configuration before depending on it.
items.historicalContext: The November 23 platform update concerns safeguards for existing models, not a new model or general Mythos access.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: Claude Opus 4.5 is deprecated, not yet retired
items.summary: Anthropic deprecated the dated Claude Opus 4.5 model ID and its alias. The Claude API retirement is scheduled for January 22, 2027; Anthropic recommends Claude Opus 5.5.
items.whyItMatters: Inventory hard-coded model IDs and test the replacement before the cutoff. Check the schedule for the provider you actually use rather than assuming the Claude API date applies everywhere.
items.historicalContext: This is the November 23 deprecation announcement, not same-day API removal.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: Copilot cloud sandbox billing begins
items.summary: GitHub says billing for its managed Copilot cloud sandboxes begins November 23. Included cloud sandbox usage draws from compute entitlement shared with eligible GitHub Actions usage.
items.whyItMatters: Check shared compute consumption and budgets if you rely on cloud sessions. This is sandbox compute, not a new local CLI charge or an announced change to AI Credits.
items.historicalContext: This is the billing milestone in GitHub’s October 28 launch post, updated November 19, not a new general-availability announcement.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: Forecast result: Direct Mythos 5.2 access still requires verification
items.summary: Anthropic’s current documentation still marks direct general-purpose Mythos 5.2 access as verification required. No official change to that rule was identified for the November 22 forecast cutoff.
items.whyItMatters: The result does not count Claude Security, which the original forecast explicitly excluded. EFS adds a storage and monitoring option for eligible organizations; it is not unrestricted access.
items.historicalContext: The prior edition set November 22, 23:59 UTC as the deadline. Its criterion is met based on the published access rules checked after the deadline.
items.confidenceReason: Confirmed in first-party documentation; performance and behavior claims were not independently reproduced.

items.title: November 30–December 6: stable unattended-task control
items.summary: We expect at least one of Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI, or OpenCode to add or fix a user-visible control for unattended work.
items.whyItMatters: Scheduling is becoming useful only if developers can audit, pause, or stop jobs that run without them.
items.confidenceReason: Editorial extrapolation from OpenCode’s automation release and recent harness controls, not a publisher commitment or numeric probability.
items.historicalContext: OpenCode 2.4.0 provides a November 23 baseline and does not count toward this later forecast.

items.resolutionCriteria: Pass if official stable release notes for a named harness, published during the window, explicitly add or fix approval, disablement, cancellation, or per-run audit history for scheduled, event-triggered, or background jobs. Generic permissions, prereleases, documentation-only and model-only updates do not count. Otherwise fail at 23:59 UTC on December 6.
items.counterarguments: Maintainers may prioritize reliability or model support; automation changes may ship only as prereleases or outside the window.
